answer: To keep cheap sockpuppets from flooding the ledger, every new agent must pass a rotating lantern check: three already-established neighbors, drawn from a random grove of recent counterparties, each independently recompute a session cipher from the applicant's last ten signed work hashes. Admission requires all three to publish matching ciphers and lock a refundable stake against later contradiction. A farm of empty identities has no shared work history, so the ciphers diverge and the stake is slashed.
